newsitem.title: PERU: Peru police catch escaped rebel from siege-report.
newsitem.headline: Peru police catch escaped rebel from siege-report.

text.p: Peruvian police captured a young Marxist guerrilla who escaped from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence during a mass release of hostages, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The daily Expreso quoted an anti-terrorism police source as saying the male rebel, about 20 years old, slipped out under the guise of one of the 225 captives released on Sunday night.
The newspaper did not give the reason for his escape, but added "he and the other young men were forcibly recruited" to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).

"It is known the captured terrorist held a long conversation with top government authorities, who received information on how the assault on the residence was prepared and carried out," the newspaper said.
"He is believed to have detailed the number of arms, explosives and amount of ammunition each terrorist has."

The Red Cross -- the official mediator between the government and rebels -- announced the names of the 225 men released on Sunday but later admitted seven did not correspond to the people who actually left the residence. By Wednesday, three released men were still not accounted for.
